title: introduce-shadow-batch-allocator-autoconfig-and-econ-prober
author: Avery Chen
description: This PR adds a new component, the Shadow Batch Allocator (SBA), and an associated CLI prober to automatically infer tenant-appropriate batching, prefill/cache defaults, and quantization suggestions via non-disruptive shadow experiments. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/prefill/quant settings per tenant to meet unit-econ targets; this manual work is error-prone and slow. SBA runs shadowed dry-runs of candidate batch shapes and quant profiles in the background, measures tail P99 latency, throughput, and model-quality proxies (logprobs/response-length heuristics), and scores trade-offs against a configurable cost model. The initial implementation focuses on tenant-scoped defaults, not on live request mutation, so it is safe for rollout and can be enabled per-tenant as an opt-in flag. Key behaviors: 1) A lightweight probe client (rw-econ probe) captures anonymized request signatures and schedules them into shadow batching runs; 2) The allocator evaluates multiple batch-shape candidates (micro, mini, pooled) and quant profiles (FP16, int8-quantized candidates) with fixed-duration trials; 3) Results are synthesized into a ranked set of recommended defaults for batching_size, prefill_kv_cache, and quant_profile with expected unit-cost delta and estimated P95/P99 impact; 4) Recommendations are exported to the Console as a suggested tenant defaults bundle and to the CLI as a dry-run JSON that operators can review before applying. Implementation notes: SBA is implemented mostly in the runtime scheduler (scheduler/shadow_allocator.go) and an opt-in controller (controller/econ_probe_controller.go). A new small telemetry bridge (telemetry/econ-shadow-metrics) emits a compact set of metrics and a summary artifact stored in the existing tenant-metadata store for review and rollouts. The PR includes unit and integration tests, a dry-run simulation harness, and an example tenant defaults bundle. Scope exclusions: does NOT auto-apply recommendations; does not modify live routing or rollback rules; does not perform model fine-tuning. Security and privacy: payloads used for shadow runs are tokenized and schema-hashed; only duration, token counts, and response-length heuristics are retained for the summary artifact. Related work: follows on ENG-2745 (batching telemetry) and ENG-3012 (quantization suggestion UI).
commits: a1b2c3d: add shadow allocator core loop and candidate evaluator
d4e5f6a: introduce econ prober CLI and probe client middleware
b7c8d9e: telemetry bridge and tenant summary artifact writer
c0ffee1: unit tests for candidate scoring and cost-model integration
deadbeef: example tenant bundle and console integration hooks
feedface: CI fixes and flake handling for integration tests
ci_checks: bench: warn (one flaky micro-bench, rerun passed)
review_comments: Priya Patel: Can we clarify the safety boundaries? Make sure the prober can't leak user content to logs. (resolved)
Avery Chen: Payloads are tokenized and we only persist schema-hashed signatures; added a privacy section in docs and unit tests for redaction (see telemetry/econ-shadow-metrics).
Marco Ruiz: The cost model looks optimistic for int8 candidates on T4 classes; please add explicit calibration samples from 2 dev tenants. (addressed)
Avery Chen: Added calibration dataset and a regression test to ensure int8 estimates are within 12% of observed costs on CI-simulated runs.
Leah Thompson: We should gate the allocator behind a feature flag and tenant opt-in. Also add a rate limiter so probes can't overload schedulers. (addressed)
Avery Chen: Feature flag added (feature.econ.shadow_allocator) and probe-client rate limiter introduced with default conservative limits; documented in ops guide.
release_notes: Add Shadow Batch Allocator and rw-econ probe: non-disruptive tenant-specific recommendations for batching, prefill, and quantization. Opt-in and behind feature flag. See docs/ops/shadow-batcher.md for rollout guidance.
notes: This PR intentionally produces recommendation artifacts only; follow-up PR will add an operator workflow to apply bundles and a gradual rollout automation. Observatory dashboards added to Console but default retention is short; customers with longer retention must enable the telemetry add-on.
